ai.name: Stripe / OpenRouter
ai.hook: Stripe's OpenRouter buy is really a bet on owning payment rails for AI usage, not model access.
insights: Ben Thompson frames it as an **Aggregation play**: whoever sits between businesses and models controls the switching cost.
Follows a week of pricing wars: **OpenRouter and Vercel both cut prices** right before the deal closed.
Signals model routing itself is becoming a commodity layer, the real value is billing and orchestration on top.
ai.for_you: If you're pricing the agency's AI stack for PT SMBs, don't build your own model router, wire into one of these layers instead and put your margin on the workflow and support, not the routing.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Third day this story develops, now with the clearest strategic read of why it matters.

ai.name: AT&T
ai.role: Enterprise AI case study, via AINews
ai.hook: AT&T routes 40% of employee AI usage to open models, cutting coding costs 56% with only 2% quality drop.
insights: Target is **60-70% open-model routing** at 45 billion tokens/day.
Hybrid routing (open model first, frontier model as fallback) is becoming the default enterprise pattern, not the exception.
Quality loss is nearly negligible at this scale, undercutting the case for always using frontier closed models.
ai.for_you: This is the exact pitch structure for your AI agency: sell PT SMBs a hybrid setup where cheap open models (Qwen3.8-27B, GLM) handle 80% of tasks and a frontier model is called only when needed, this is your cost story in sales calls.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Concrete enterprise numbers, rare in a week of vague model releases.

ai.name: Ornith-1.5
ai.hook: New MIT-licensed model family ships in 9B, 35B MoE, and 397B MoE sizes with self-improvement built in.
insights: Full quantized format support out of the box: **FP8, GGUF, MLX, NVFP4**.
Qwen3.8-27B GGUFs with Dynamic V3 quantization hit **10% higher accuracy**, and 1-bit quant retains 77% of BF16 accuracy while fitting in **8GB RAM**.
Small quantized models running well on consumer RAM keeps closing the gap with cloud inference costs.
ai.for_you: The 9B dense variant, quantized, is a candidate for a local/offline demo for SMB clients who are nervous about sending data to the cloud, worth a 30-minute test on your own machine before pitching it as a feature.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Only genuinely new open model release in the batch beyond GLM-5.3, already covered.

ai.name: Nathan Lambert
ai.hook: Ships a full post-training textbook after years documenting how open models actually get trained.
insights: Covers the concrete mechanics of post-training: RLHF variants, data curation, evaluation loops.
Positioned as the reference for anyone who wants to actually understand model behavior, not just use an API.
Companion post asks how long until AI can write a technically rigorous textbook better than a human expert.
ai.for_you: Not urgent for the agency, but this is the single best resource this month if you want to move from 'PM who prompts well' to genuinely fluent in why models behave the way they do.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Rare, substantive long-form release amid a week of incremental model news.

video.title: How to get the best AI Prompts

ai.name: ChatGPT Search
ai.hook: ChatGPT search now runs site:operator queries at scale, quietly becoming a real search engine.
insights: New 'GEO' (Generative Engine Optimization) industry is forming around tracking how sites appear in chatbot answers.
Promptwatch and similar tools now publish aggregate reports on brand visibility inside ChatGPT/Claude/Gemini responses.
This mirrors early SEO, but the ranking signal is now an LLM's retrieval behavior, not a search index.
ai.for_you: Worth testing this week: search how your agency and your clients' businesses show up when prompted inside ChatGPT, this could become a real service line (GEO audits for PT SMBs) before anyone local is offering it.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Emerging channel with a concrete, sellable angle nobody local is touching yet.

video.title: ChatGPT now has a search engine?!🚀📈 #ai #chatgpt #seo #aiautomation #artificialintelligence

ai.name: Alex Krentsel
ai.role: UC Berkeley / Google Research · Latent Space podcast
ai.hook: Exo agent can see its own code and logs, letting it clone and improve itself incrementally.
insights: Unlike most agents that only update memory, Exo can rewrite prompts, tooling, and its own harness policy.
It maintains a canonical event log it cannot alter, preventing recursive improvement loops from spiraling.
Framed as a systems approach to recursive self-improvement, not just a smarter chatbot wrapper.
ai.for_you: No direct action for the agency this week, this is research-grade infrastructure, but worth watching as the pattern (agents that log and audit their own changes) will likely become the safety standard you'll need to explain to cautious SMB clients.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Deepest technical explainer on a story that's been trending three days running.

build_this.name: Vomit
build_this.what_it_is: A small tool that pipes noisy Claude Code token output through a second cheap LLM to clean it up before you read it.
build_this.why_try_it: You're using Claude Code daily to get more technically fluent, this could cut the noise-reading tax and is a 20-minute install to test on your own agency codebase this week.

build_this.name: MIDI Autocomplete (125M on-device model)
build_this.what_it_is: A tiny 125M parameter model trained to autocomplete piano playing, runs entirely on-device.
build_this.why_try_it: Not for the agency, but directly relevant to the yoga/meditation platform: it's a working example of a small, cheap, purpose-trained model for a creative/wellness domain, worth reading the writeup as a template if you ever want a bespoke small model (e.g. breath-pattern or pose feedback) instead of calling a frontier API.

build_this.name: PostHog
build_this.what_it_is: Open-source product analytics platform with AI observability, session replay, and an MCP interface you can steer from Slack or the web.
build_this.why_try_it: Worth self-hosting or trialing on the yoga platform or a micro-SaaS this week to get real usage data before you build more features blind, its MCP support also means you could let an agent query your own product analytics directly.
